- **ep**: Giuffre was recruited around 2000 while working as a spa attendant at Mar-a-Lago, aged sixteen. She became the case's most prominent public accuser, and her sworn allegations in civil litigation produced much of the documentary record this module rests on. She stated that Trump, whose property it was, did not participate in any misconduct and was friendly to her — reported here because the module applies its standard in both directions.

- **ep**: He was released in July 2009, a registered sex offender with a conviction for procuring a minor for prostitution. He settled with Giuffre for $500,000 the same year. His social and financial life substantially resumed. Nothing in the public record from this point can be attributed to ignorance: his status was a matter of public registry.
- **ep**: Giuffre was recruited at Mar-a-Lago as a teenager working as a spa attendant, and became the most prominent public accuser in the case. Her sworn allegations, made in litigation under penalty of perjury and tested across years of civil proceedings, produced the documentary record that most of this module rests on — including the depositions and exhibits released through her litigation. She settled with Epstein for $500,000 in 2009 and sued Prince Andrew in 2021, settling in February 2022. Her posthumous memoir, Nobody's Girl, was published in October 2025. She died by suicide in April 2025, aged 41. Her family's statement when Andrew lost his titles quoted her own words: he knows what happened, I know what happened, and there is only one of us telling the truth.
- **ep**: The standard this module applies: an individual is named in connection with alleged conduct where a court record, sworn testimony, or a charging document does so — with the tier stated. Virginia Giuffre's sworn allegations, made in litigation under penalty of perjury and tested in civil proceedings, are a different evidentiary category from a manifest entry, and are treated as such. So are Marra's findings. So is the Maxwell verdict. The distinction is not between people who deserve protection and people who don't. It is between documents that establish conduct and documents that establish presence.
- **ep**: A court reached a result. Maxwell's conviction on five counts is the only criminal verdict. Andrew's 2022 settlement of Giuffre's civil suit is adjudicated in a weaker sense — a case resolved by agreement without admission, which is a documented legal event and not a finding of liability. This tier is small, and its smallness after two decades of investigation is itself one of the module's findings.
- **ep**: A named accuser has alleged specific conduct by a specific person, on the record, in a proceeding where lying carries criminal exposure. Giuffre's allegations against Andrew sit here, as do the trial witnesses' accounts against Maxwell. This is materially stronger than a media claim and materially weaker than a verdict: it is an allegation that has been formally made and, in most instances here, never tested at trial because no trial occurred.
- **ep**: The clearest demonstration that this discipline matters. Giuffre named Alan Dershowitz in litigation; he denied it and countersued; in 2022 the parties settled with both withdrawing their claims, and Giuffre stated she may have made a mistake in identifying him. This module reports that outcome and names no one on the strength of the original allegation. It is included because it is the strongest available argument for the standard: a sworn allegation from the most credible accuser in the case was later withdrawn by the accuser herself, in a subject where dozens of names circulate on far less.
- **ep**: Giuffre alleged in sworn litigation that she was trafficked to Andrew and had sexual encounters with him on three occasions, the first when she was seventeen. She sued him in 2021 in the Southern District of New York. He has consistently and vigorously denied the accusations, and continued denying them in his October 2025 statement. Her posthumous memoir, published in October 2025, set out her account in detail. This is a sworn allegation that was never tested at trial, and both of those facts belong in any honest account of it.
- **ep**: A photograph taken in 2001 at Maxwell's London townhouse showing Andrew with his arm around a then-teenage Giuffre, with Maxwell behind them. Released with court documents, it became the single most reproduced image in the case. Andrew questioned its authenticity in his 2019 BBC Newsnight interview — an appearance widely regarded as catastrophic for him, in which he offered explanations that were subsequently contradicted. The photograph does not establish conduct. It establishes that the three were together, which he had disputed.
- **ep**: Andrew settled Giuffre's civil suit in February 2022 for an undisclosed sum widely reported as substantial, expressing regret for his association with Epstein without admitting guilt or offering an explicit apology. The same structure as the bank settlements: money moves, no finding is entered, and the underlying question stays formally open. - **ep**: On October 17, 2025 Andrew announced he would stop using his titles.
